feature.caustica.bloom.description: Spread light from bright areas into their surroundings.
caustica.screen.title: CAUSTICA
caustica.setting.enabled.tooltip: Replace the raster renderer with the path tracer. Turning this off returns Minecraft to vanilla rendering.
caustica.setting.composite.max-bounces.t: Maximum secondary bounces after the primary hit. Higher captures more indirect light at more cost.
caustica.setting.composite.water-waves.t: Animate water-surface normals for moving wave highlights.
caustica.setting.tonemap.gamma.tooltip: Post-transform luminance gamma. Below 1 brightens shadows and midtones while preserving black, white, and colour ratios.
caustica.setting.denoising.route.tooltip: Choose raw path tracing, NRD temporal denoising, or DLSS Ray Reconstruction.
caustica.setting.denoising.method.toolti: Choose which NRD denoiser to use with the temporal denoising route.
caustica.setting.dlss-rr.quality.tooltip: Lower modes render fewer pixels and upscale harder for framerate; higher modes render more for sharpness.
caustica.setting.dlss-sr.quality.tooltip: Choose the render resolution used before NRD output is reconstructed to display resolution.
caustica.setting.frame-generation.enable: Generate intermediate frames with DLSS. Raises framerate without lowering latency.
caustica.setting.reflex.enabled.tooltip: Reduce input latency by pacing frame submission. Requires supported NVIDIA hardware.
caustica.setting.exposure.mode.tooltip: Auto adapts to scene luminance; Manual holds the exposure value directly.
caustica.setting.exposure.manual-ev.tool: Positive values brighten; negative values darken. Sets exposure in Manual and adjusts automatic exposure in Auto.
caustica.setting.hdr.enabled.tooltip: Recreate the swapchain for HDR (ST.2084/PQ) output. Requires operating system and display support.
caustica.setting.hdr.ui-nits.tooltip: Absolute brightness, in nits, given to SDR-authored UI on an HDR display.
caustica.setting.hdr.peak-nits.tooltip: Brightness, in nits, highlights roll off toward. Set this to your display's peak HDR brightness; ACES 2.0 renders through the nearest of its 500, 1000, 2000, and 4000 nit LUTs.
caustica.setting.sdr.tone-mapper.tooltip: Display rendering operator for SDR output. ACES 2.0 renders through the reference LUTs with the scene look; the other mappers run on the exposed scene-linear signal and own their complete display rendering.
caustica.setting.hdr.tone-mapper.tooltip: Display rendering operator for HDR output. ACES 2.0 renders through the reference LUTs; the other mappers render paper-white-referred colour analytically toward the display peak.
caustica.setting.hdr.paper-white-nits.to: Brightness, in nits, given to diffuse white by the analytic HDR tone mappers. Highlights roll off from here toward the display peak.
caustica.setting.entities.enabled.toolti: Include entities and block entities in the traced scene.
caustica.setting.particles.enabled.toolt: Draw particles as camera-ray billboards inside the traced scene.
caustica.setting.entities.glow.enabled.t: Draw the vanilla Glowing-effect outline, through walls, around glowing entities.
caustica.setting.overlay.block-outline.e: Draw the selection outline around the block you are looking at.
caustica.setting.composite.debug-view.to: Inspect ray-tracing buffers and exposure diagnostics after the normal frame has rendered.
caustica.setting.screenshots.exr-enabled: Save a scene-linear ACEScg EXR alongside the normal PNG when you take a screenshot.
caustica.option.caustica.bloom.bloom.ena: Bleed light from bright areas into their surroundings.
caustica.option.caustica.bloom.bloom.str: Brightness of the glow around bright areas.
caustica.option.caustica.bloom.bloom.thr: Scene-linear luminance a pixel must exceed before it blooms.
caustica.option.caustica.bloom.bloom.sof: Softens the threshold so pixels fade into blooming instead of snapping.
caustica.option.caustica.bloom.bloom.rad: How far the glow spreads around bright areas.
caustica.option.caustica.bloom.bloom.lev: Number of blur levels. More levels spread the glow farther across the screen.
caustica.option.caustica.minecraft.sky.s: How far south of overhead the sun sits at noon, in degrees. Higher gives longer shadows year-round.
Apparent radius of the sun as a light source, in degrees. Larger softens shadow edges.
caustica.option.caustica.minecraft.sky.m: Apparent radius of the moon as a light source, in degrees.
caustica.option.caustica.minecraft.sky.s: How large the sun sprite is drawn, in degrees. Does not change how much light it casts.
caustica.option.caustica.minecraft.sky.m: How large the moon sprite is drawn, in degrees.
caustica.option.caustica.minecraft.sky.g: How much light the ground bounces back into the sky. Raising it brightens the whole atmosphere.
caustica.option.caustica.minecraft.sky.h: How far the horizon is blurred, in degrees, to hide the hard edge of the sky model.
caustica.option.caustica.minecraft.fog.e: Add drifting mist that varies with time of day, terrain height, and biome.
caustica.option.caustica.minecraft.fog.d: Scale the thickness of the mist. Higher values reduce visibility.
caustica.option.caustica.minecraft.fog.r: Lower values sharpen fog around terrain and trees at a higher GPU cost.
caustica.option.caustica.minecraft.fog.s: Higher values reduce integration noise at a higher GPU cost.
caustica.option.caustica.minecraft.fog.d: 0: Normal image. 1: Fog transmittance. 2: Scattered light.
